clue.text: Islander's son with a complaint

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
a moan is a complaint; 'with' just joins it on

explanation.surface: A man from some island and his son are grumbling about something.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Samoa, the Pacific island nation, is an islander.

clue.text: Parson last to be moved in change in order

indicators.note: letters that are moved get shifted about into new positions

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman is finally being relocated as part of a reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adverb about the parson's turn, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A transposal is the act of swapping things round, an alteration of their sequence.

clue.text: That man interrupts canine with a doggy treat?

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: C is the dental shorthand for a canine tooth
a pronoun for 'that man'
W is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Some man butts in on a dog that is being given a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a dental formula C stands for canine; with W for 'with' it frames HE. The question mark flags that a chew is a treat for a dog rather than doggy in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A chew is a toy or snack given to dogs to gnaw on, a classic pet reward.

clue.text: Hissing excuses upset conservation group

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: alibis are excuses
the National Trust, a British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Someone hisses with displeasure at excuses that have annoyed a conservation body.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is the British charity that looks after historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibilant describes sounds made with a hiss, like s and sh.

clue.text: Seaman not entirely kind about trouble

indicators.note: not entirely means a word stops short of its full length
about means going round, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: sort, a kind, without its final letter
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A seaman who is not altogether kind about some trouble on board.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor is a seaman, someone who works on ships.

clue.text: Target of coastal erosion? Absolutely true, as heard on the radio

indicators.note: radio is a medium for listening, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: literal, as in literally true, sounds much like the shore word

explanation.surface: A broadcast insists that the coast really is being eaten away.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the shore zone is what coastal erosion attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The littoral is the region of shore beside the sea, which waves wear away.

clue.text: Catching leaders in head office agreeing

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the opening letters of head and office
OK-ing, giving the OK, is agreeing

explanation.surface: Head office bosses are caught agreeing among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: HO is also the usual abbreviation for head office.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooking a fish is catching it on a hook.

clue.text: Finished half of Beatles LP, getting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
only half of the album title survives, the rest is dropped

parts.note: Revolver is a 1966 Beatles album

explanation.surface: Someone stops partway through a Beatles record and stands up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the title is kept, then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it has ended or been completed.

clue.text: Attractive opportunity opening finally after merchandise running short

indicators.note: running short means lacking something at the end

parts.note: goods, merchandise, cut short by one letter
a look-in is a chance or opportunity

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word beside it

parts.note: the final letter of opening

explanation.surface: A tempting business chance arrives at last after stock has run low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the opportunity piece behind the merchandise piece, even though the clue mentions it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attractive is pleasing in appearance, handsome or pretty.

clue.text: Old busybody, left-winger, holding text for you

indicators.note: holding means gripping something inside

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: An elderly meddler, a radical leftie, clutching a message meant for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old trout' is British slang for a disagreeable or interfering older woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout, usually as old trout, is an informal insult for a meddling, crabby older woman.

clue.text: Notes United fans as biased

indicators.note: to fan is to spread out, scattering the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A report observes that football supporters of United are partisan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' looks like a noun for supporters, but here it is a verb meaning spreads out.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendentious argument promotes one viewpoint, showing partiality.

clue.text: Former lover in charge amongst women active in US state

indicators.note: amongst means placed within a group, so one piece sits inside
active letters are on the move, stirring into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
an ex is a former partner
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An ex now runs things among energetic women in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: New Mexico is one of the fifty states, in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Fool with no work accepting reduction in revenue, perhaps at first

indicators.note: a reduction means the word is trimmed of its end
accepting means taking something in

parts.note: taken as written
income, revenue, with its tail cut off

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of perhaps
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An idiot without a job takes a pay cut, perhaps from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revenue' with 'reduction' is a deletion signal, not a money story; the trimmed word and the P sit just after the first letter of the outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A nincompoop is a silly or stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Hope to stay limber — using this?

definitions.text: Hope to stay limber — using this?

indicators.note: limber means supple and flexible, so the letters bend into new shape

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wanting to stay supple asks whether this treatment helps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: people who want to keep supple might use this therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy manipulates bones and muscles, a therapy aimed at keeping the body flexible.

clue.text: Mate carrying one component of wishing well?

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A friend lugging one part of a wishing well.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a wishing well often has a bucket on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is a bucket, which hangs from the winch of a traditional well.

clue.text: Fashion supplier, one not so clever yesterday in Paris

parts.note: a clot is a dimwit
hier is French for yesterday

explanation.surface: A fashion seller, a bit dim, was in Paris yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Paris' tells the solver to give yesterday in French. A clot is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier makes or sells garments, so supplies fashion.

clue.text: Cut back, limiting transactions a bit more

indicators.note: limiting means fencing in on both sides
back means turned round to read the other way

parts.note: to axe is to cut

indicators.note: only a bit of the word is used, its opening, the rest dropped

parts.note: just the start of this word is kept

explanation.surface: Spending is cut back, restricting dealings a little more.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two letters of transactions sit inside AXE reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, over and above, so serves as an adjective for more.

clue.text: New cryptic clue, not last one among three, for Shakespearean drunk

indicators.note: not the last one means the final letter of the word is lost
among means placed in the midst of something

parts.note: a trio is a group of three
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the word clue without its last letter

explanation.surface: A setter's fresh tricky clue, minus one, among three others, for a tipsy Shakespeare character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not last one' applies to clue alone: the word loses its final letter before being scrambled.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinculo is the drunken jester in The Tempest, who falls in with Stephano and Caliban.

clue.text: Team to go down

definitions.meaning: second meaning: what the sun does at dusk

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a team being relegated, but the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a group of people and also to sink below the horizon, as the sun does.

clue.text: Toilet getting dry internally? It's something of a gamble

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: loo is British slang for toilet
TT stands for teetotal, meaning dry

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a toilet will dry out inside is a bit of a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery or bingo-style game of chance, a kind of wager.

clue.text: Dahl character, not the full pair? The very thing

indicators.note: not the full means part of the word is missing at the end

parts.note: two, a pair, cut short
'that's it!' means the very thing

explanation.surface: One of Roald Dahl's duo, not both of them, is just the thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nudges toward The Twits, whose pair is Mr and Mrs Twit; the wordplay works on 'pair' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr and Mrs Twit are the nasty couple in Roald Dahl's book The Twits, so either one is a character called Twit.

clue.text: High clouds: I start getting perturbed after a lot at sea

indicators.note: perturbed means agitated and thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone startled by high clouds after a long time on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged A LOT first.
explanation.definitionFit: Altostrati are grey sheet clouds of the middle-to-upper atmosphere, the plural of altostratus.

clue.text: Experts securing very good high points

indicators.note: securing means holding something fast inside

parts.note: aces are experts
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good

explanation.surface: Specialists reaching some excellent peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Apices is the plural of apex, a tip or summit.

clue.text: Film's star to support a cause, though not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to plead a cause is to argue for it

explanation.surface: A movie star backing a campaign, though not initially.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead is the principal role, so the film's main actor.

clue.text: Coffer artist depicted with golden band

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a coffer is a chest
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A treasure box painted by an artist alongside a golden ribbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a strip of gold to go with the coffer, but it is a group of musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians, i.e. a band.

clue.text: Source of wood, support for golfer crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means spanning over, so the outer piece straddles the inner

parts.note: a tee holds the golf ball up
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A golfer's peg, made of wood, that has to carry over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' suggests a golf club, but it means timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber comes from felled trees.

clue.text: First couple heading off assessing cost of decoration

indicators.note: the first couple of letters go away from the front

parts.note: pricing is assessing a cost

explanation.surface: A pair of people leaving first to work out what the decorating will cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is the sugary coating used to decorate cakes.

clue.text: Spot, or half-spot, porter's office

indicators.note: half means only part of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: the first half of spot
a porter's lodge is the gatehouse office of a college

explanation.surface: A spot, or a small spot, at the porter's lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word appears twice: first as the definition, then as the fodder to be halved.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a blot or irregular mark, i.e. a spot.

clue.text: Skin disease: woman's source of annoyance, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
pest, a source of annoyance, missing its end

explanation.surface: A woman's irritating complaint turns out to be a skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Herpes is a viral infection causing blisters on the skin.
